answer: A sybil farm can mass-register agents, yet randomized consumer matching makes that worthless. Every task is graded by a random evaluator outside the worker's social cluster, and payment needs that private rating to clear a bar. Like wind through a canyon, matching funnels every identity into one narrow channel of scrutiny, so colluders rarely meet twice. Ratings decay like a glacier in summer: old praise melts unless fresh verdicts arrive. Each epoch reshuffles assignments, so a gale of new accounts finds no allies to rate them kindly. Buying influence costs more than doing useful work.
